newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT plans to cut long-distance rates in February.
newsitem.headline: NTT plans to cut long-distance rates in February.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp said on Thursday it had applied to the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry to cut its long-distance call rates to 110 yen per three minutes from the current 140 yen in February.
The cut will push down NTT's revenues by 60 billion yen in the initial year after the rate decrease, the company said.

The rate cut will reduce daytime charges for the longest-distance domestic calls of more than 100 km, which are higher than those of other countries, NTT president Junichiro Miyazu said in a recent news conference.
Rival long-distance operators such as DDI Corp and Japan Telecom Co, as well as cellular phone operators, are expected to follow suit soon.
